test_title: RRB Technician Grade III Official Paper (Held On: 29 Dec, 2024 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: A shopkeeper lists the price of a fan at 22% above its cost price and offers a 15% discount on its list price. What is the cost price (in Rs. ) of the fan if he sells it at Rs. 5,185?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the **Cost Price (CP)** be 100 units.

**Marked Price (MP)** = 100 + 22% of 100 = 122 units.

**Selling Price (SP)** = 122 × (100 − 15) ÷ 100 = 122 × 0.85 = 103.7 units.

Given SP = Rs. 5,185 ⇒ 103.7 units = 5185.

CP (100 units) = (5185 ÷ 103.7) × 100 = 50 × 100 = Rs. 5000.

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 5000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Markup% = 22%, Discount% = 15%, **Selling Price (SP)** = Rs. 5,185.

**Formulas:** MP = CP × (100 + Markup%) ÷ 100 | SP = MP × (100 − Discount%) ÷ 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/987ebc3f53da6ff55b3b244194ea2dfff763d08928d1e49c8b9466357fed218d.png] 

⇒ Let CP be x.

⇒ MP = x × (122 ÷ 100) = 1.22x.

⇒ SP = 1.22x × (85 ÷ 100) = 5185.

⇒ 1.037x = 5185.

⇒ x = 5185 ÷ 1.037 = 5000.

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 5000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Markup and Discount Relation

Profit% = Markup% − Discount% − (Markup × Discount ÷ 100). This helps find net profit quickly.

Marked Price Formula

CP ÷ MP = (100 − Discount%) ÷ (100 + Profit%). This ratio links CP and MP directly.</p
